add_players.name: Drew Valentine
add_players.accolades: Played for his father, coach Carlton Valentine, at Sexton; older brother of Denzel Valentine. Became Oakland's winningest player (87 wins, two NCAA Tournaments). Named Loyola Chicago head coach in 2021 at age 30, the youngest in Division I; led the Ramblers to the 2022 NCAA Tournament and a share of the 2023-24 Atlantic 10 regular-season title.

add_players.name: Paul Crosby
add_players.accolades: 6-foot-8 forward. Sophomore on Holt's 2005 Class A state champions (all-state honorable mention). As a senior averaged 18.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 3.2 blocks and was the Lansing State Journal Player of the Year; first-team AP all-state; rated Michigan's No. 1 power forward by PrepSpotlight. Signed with Toledo.
add_players.college: Navarro College (2007-09); Mississippi Valley State (2010-12): 2012 SWAC Player of the Year, two-time first-team All-SWAC, AP honorable mention All-American, 2012 NCAA Tournament
add_players.pro: Undrafted in 2012. Played in Uruguay (Montevideo), Brazil (Minas), Indonesia (Laskar Dreya) and Chile (CD Talca); 2013 NBA D-League draft pick.

add_players.name: Trevor Manuel
add_players.accolades: 6-foot-9 forward. Class A all-state as an Everett senior in 2014-15 (21.9 points a game); ESPN ranked him the No. 3 player in Michigan. Won the 2011-12 state title as a freshman at Lansing Sexton and was Class B all-state there as a sophomore, then played a season at Oak Hill Academy.
add_players.college: Oregon (2015); Loyola Marymount; Olivet (All-MIAA first team, 2019)

add_players.name: Clyde McKinney Jr.
add_players.accolades: Guard on Everett's 2004 Class A state champions. Had 6 points, 3 assists and 2 steals in the 69-64 semifinal win over Pontiac Northern, then 8 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists in the 60-51 final over Flint Carman-Ainsworth at Breslin Center.

tournament_summary.note: District titles through 2014-15 from michigan-football.com; 2025-26 district (64-39 over Ionia) from the Portland Beacon.
Beat Ionia 75-54 in the 1986 regional final.

add_players.name: Alex Gauna
add_players.accolades: 6-foot-9, 230-pound forward. Averaged 16.5 points, 10.4 rebounds and 2.4 blocks as a junior and 15.4 points and 4.2 blocks as a sophomore. Fourth-team Class B all-state (Detroit Free Press); Lansing State Journal all-area. Ranked in the national top 150 by Scout and Rivals.

add_players.name: Sean Romsek
add_players.accolades: Four-year starter under coach Fred Hackett and Fowlerville's all-time leading scorer (1,400+ points). 2006-07 Livingston County Player of the Year, three-time all-conference, all-state honorable mention; led two district title teams.
